items.title: Sony Music’s AI Slop and Deepfakes Crackdown Intensifies — Soundalike Track Removal Requests Reportedly Top 250,000
items.summary: Sony Music’s AI deepfakes crackdown is intensifying: As of September’s end, the major label had fired off north of 250,000 cumulative soundalike-track takedown demands. That concrete figure came to light in a recent Financial Times piece, which pointed to over 260,000 deepfake takedown requests submitted to various “pl…

items.title: Japanese court says voice is protected by publicity rights; US appeals court says AI training is not fair use
items.summary: There have been two judgments this week of relevance to the ongoing AI debates in the music industry. A Japanese court ruled that publicity rights allow performers to stop unapproved AI voice clones. Meanwhile a US appeals court ruled against an AI company that used the good old fair use defence

items.title: Sony Music has now filed 260k takedowns of AI-deepfake tracks
items.summary: In March 2025, Sony Music said that it had successfully gotten more than 75k AI-generated deepfakes of its artists from various online platforms. A year later, in March 2026, the company said that it had now filed more than 135k of these takedown notices. The post is from Music Ally .

items.title: ‘The Song Is Non-Negotiable’: Indie Music Giants Unite to Force a Fair Licensing Framework
items.summary: Indie publishing orgs IMPF and IMPEL have outlined a licensing framework for generative AI to create a fair and sustainable market for the future. Independent music publishing organizations IMPEL and IMPF have now issued a licensing framework for generative AI based on several key principles that will ensure song copyr…

items.title: Historic ruling on 'fair use' and AI may help Nashville songwriters
Trump’s DoJ was biased and wrong about ‘fair use’, say news orgs in OpenAI dispute
items.summary: Many of the music industry’s AI legal battles swing on whether or not AI training is ‘fair use’ under US copyright law. Donald Trump’s DoJ recently intervened in a dispute between newspapers and OpenAI insisting AI training is fair use. The newspapers have responded, explaining why the DoJ is wrong

items.title: Sony Music has now asked platforms to remove more than 260,000 AI deepfakes imitating artists like Harry Styles, Adele, and Michael Jackson
items.summary: Sony told the Financial Times that the fight against AI tracks impersonating artists such as Harry Styles and Adele is "becoming an uphill struggle." Source

items.title: Don’t say collusion: “no evidence of misconduct or conflict of interest” say major labels and publishers about their Phono V physical negotiations
items.summary: The US Copyright Royalty Board is reviewing what mechanical royalties songwriters and publishers should receive from 2028. It’s labels who pay mechanical royalties on physical records, and the major labels are keen to stress they aren’t colluding with the major publishers to keep the rates down

tip.title: Antes de firmar, revisa la reversión de derechos
tip.body: La pregunta clave de cualquier contrato no es cuánto te dan hoy, sino cuándo y cómo recuperas tu obra. Si no hay cláusula de reversión, estás cediendo por el plazo completo.

tip.title: Before signing, check the reversion clause
tip.body: The key question in any deal isn't what you get today —it's when and how you get your work back. With no reversion clause, you're assigning for the full term.
